name: NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 Blackwell GPU (per GPU, dense peaks)
scope: one Blackwell GPU within a GB200 Grace Blackwell Superchip; not the two-GPU Superchip or HGX B200

memory_capacity_provenance.basis: measured device capacity override supplied by the cluster preflight
memory_capacity_provenance.scope: observed target device, not an inference from NVIDIA marketing capacity

compute_provenance.basis: NVIDIA published GB200 NVL72 specification; theoretical peak, not calibrated sustained performance
compute_provenance.normalization: Superchip contains two GPUs. Divide the listed Superchip Tensor Core sparse rate by two GPUs and then by two for dense. Divide scalar FP32/FP64 rates only by two GPUs.
compute_provenance.dense_bfloat16_derivation: 10 PFLOP/s sparse per Superchip / 2 GPUs / 2 = 2.5 PFLOP/s dense per GPU
compute_provenance.dense_fp8_derivation: 20 PFLOP/s sparse per Superchip / 2 GPUs / 2 = 5 PFLOP/s dense per GPU
compute_provenance.hbm_derivation: 16 TB/s per Superchip / 2 GPUs = 8 TB/s per GPU; decimal TB = 10^12 bytes
compute_provenance.execution_precision: float32 uses scalar FP32 peak; TF32 is only selected by an explicit tf32 execution-dtype event. FP8 rates apply to actual FP8 Tensor Core arithmetic, not storage dtype alone.
compute_provenance.sparse_policy: Sparse rates are reference metadata only. Current runtime rejects sparse work; it never substitutes a sparse rate for dense work.

assumptions: Published NVLink aggregate interface bandwidth is not assumed to equal effective collective payload throughput.
No rank placement, topology, collective algorithm, startup latency, NCCL efficiency or network contention is inferred.
Collective analytical timing requires a separate explicit effective bandwidth assumption; calibrated timing requires exact measured entries.

sources.title: NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 official specifications
sources.supports: Two GPUs per Superchip; sparse versus dense Tensor Core footnote; FP32/FP64; HBM bandwidth and published capacity; NVLink interface bandwidth

sources.title: NVIDIA GB200 NVL multi-node tuning guide: platform overview
sources.supports: GB200/NVL72 architecture and published NVLink bandwidth; no measured collective efficiency supplied

limitations: All peak rates are optimistic theoretical roofline ceilings; kernel efficiency and launch overhead are not calibrated.
Clock, power and thermal limits of the measured cluster can change sustained rates.
Capacity override is device-specific; remeasure for other hardware or MIG configurations.
HBM traffic in dispatch traces is logical tensor payload and is not measured DRAM traffic.
